nodes.question: Does the edited image establish that the requested black DVD has become a white DVD?
nodes.criteria: Inspect the edited endpoint first, then compare with the source to establish which object the observation concerns. Pass if visible evidence establishes that the requested source DVD has a white edited counterpart identifiable as a DVD. Fail if a reliably matched counterpart visibly does not meet that endpoint. Unknown if target selection, correspondence, color, or DVD identity leaves completion unresolved. Identify the source object and edited counterpart and cite the scene relationships or object features supporting the match. The central printed rectangular source item is a candidate locator, not a required preserved case or silhouette. Consider the separate right-hand object without automatically treating it as the DVD. Whiteness alone does not prove correspondence, and changed shape alone does not disprove it. DVD identity may be supported by appearance and scene context; do not demand readable labels or a visually provable DVD-versus-CD distinction.
nodes.binding: The black DVD requested in the source image and its corresponding edited object, not any white object selected solely because it resembles a disc.

nodes.question: Does comparison establish any actual whitening of the requested source DVD?
nodes.criteria: Inspect both images independently, identifying the requested source target and the counterpart used for comparison. Pass if reliable comparison establishes some black-to-white surface-color change on that target. Fail only if reliable comparison establishes no requested whitening, such as the target remaining black without any whitening. Unknown if target selection, correspondence, or color comparison is insufficient. Report the target locations, matching evidence, and observed color change or lack of change. When progress is established, describe whether the surface is fully white, partly white, or intermediate, and any visible evidence relevant to whether it remains a DVD. Do not infer no progress from an unmatched candidate, target disappearance, or changed object count. Changes to the shoe or another object are not requested progress. An uncertain earlier endpoint observation does not prevent this independent inspection.
nodes.binding: The original black DVD specified by the instruction, compared with its reliably corresponding edited target; neither the central candidate nor the right-hand candidate is selected by whiteness alone.

nodes.question: Change the black DVD to white while retaining its identity as a DVD.
nodes.criteria: Compose explicit evidence about the same requested source target, not a count of support passes. Return complete when either observation supplies sufficient evidence that the source black DVD became a white DVD; a grounded s1 pass establishes this endpoint without requiring a separate s2 pass. Return partial when comparison establishes actual whitening and also establishes that the requested endpoint is unmet, such as an intermediate or partly white surface or a white counterpart visibly no longer identifiable as a DVD. Return absent when reliable target-specific comparison establishes no requested whitening. A grounded s2 fail can establish absence without an s1 pass, but only when its evidence identifies the source target, establishes correspondence, and describes the lack of whitening. Neither an endpoint failure nor an unrelated white object establishes absence by itself. Unknown, skipped, or invalid observations add no affirmative fact and are not failures; they need not block an outcome independently established by the other observation. If necessary target-specific evidence remains missing, progress is known but completion remains uncertain, or observations contain an unresolved factual contradiction, return unknown. Do not use the reference label to settle visual uncertainty.
nodes.binding: Target: The DVD is visibly white rather than black.. Reference: The black DVD in the input image..

program.checker_template:
Execute ONE saved check. You receive no reference label or optimization feedback. Return status, evidence, reported confidence (0..1 or null), and used_dependency_ids naming every supplied context check_id exactly once in saved order.
Supports receive source and edited images. Answer only the saved proposition using its binding and criteria. Use pass/fail/unknown. Context is advisory unless listed in required_dependencies. A negative context observation is usable evidence. Unknown, skipped, or invalid context is not a failure and must not stop an independent image inspection. Inspect the images yourself; do not repeat a parent's answer. Return unknown when the relevant fact cannot be established. Confidence reports confidence in this answer, not calibrated correctness.
Fulfillment receives NO images. Use only saved support evidence, original instruction/rubric and frozen composition criteria. Return complete/partial/absent/unknown. Supporting passes answer specific propositions, not a count of completed edits. Their polarity can differ. Apply saved alternatives: optional uncertainty need not prevent a known outcome, but a required unresolved fact makes that outcome unresolved. Never invent a visual fact or convert missing evidence into failure. A conditional skip is not non-applicability. All applicable requested outcomes complete gives yes; no requested progress gives no; known progress short of completion gives partial. Unrelated changes are not progress.

observations.evidence: The source’s central printed rectangular item is a plausible DVD case, while the separate right-hand object is a black disc-like item. In the edited image, the central item is gone and two white discs appear: one near the center and one over the right-hand object. The images do not establish which, if either, corresponds to the requested DVD, so the requested transformation cannot be confirmed or ruled out.

The source image shows a small rectangular, printed object near the center, not an identifiable black DVD. The edited image contains two white disc-like objects, one near the center and one to the right, but neither can be reliably matched to the source object. Their whiteness alone does not establish that the requested DVD was whitened.

Neither observation reliably identifies the source black DVD or establishes which edited white disc, if any, corresponds to it. The requested whitening and retention of DVD identity therefore cannot be confirmed or ruled out.
